title: Marlowe agtech remote-sensor inference notes
content:
Meeting: Marlowe AgTech pilot kick-off (remote sensor inference)
Date: 2025-09-03 (initial capture) / updated 2025-10-08
Attendees: Sofia Li (Redwood), Marcus Patel (Redwood), Elena Rodriguez (solutions), Tom Hale (Marlowe CTO), Priya Sen (Marlowe Edge Eng), Aaron Liu (Marlowe Infra)
Purpose: capture constraints, high-level architecture options, immediate risks/gotchas, and define next actions for an on-field deployment of LLM-based anomaly summarization on remote soil/humidity sensors.

---
High level customer background
- Marlowe operates 18k remote sensors across distributed farms in US Midwest and Chile. Devices are low-power ARM boxes with intermittent LTE.
- Current edge pipeline: sensor -> local aggregator (Raspberry Pi 4/ARM64) -> periodic uplink to central (AWS).
- Goal: do short-form anomaly summarization and triage at the edge (generate human readable bullet summaries of outlier events), reduce uplink cost and alert noise.
- Security/compliance: no raw telemetry may leave the regional gateway for certain customers; must support VPC-like isolation or per-customer private deploy.

Non-functional constraints (from call)
- Latency: 95th percentile < 1.2s for on-edge summary generation when triggered. If using gateway (near-edge), target < 500ms.
- Model size ceiling for on-device: < 600MB compressed quantized (RAM limited to ~1.5GB).
- Uplink budget: must reduce monthly payload by >= 60% for pilot farms.
- Availability: devices lose LTE for hours; need offline stable behavior and queueing for syncs.

Primary functional requirements
1) Input: short TSV of sensor readings (~12 readings, 6 metrics) + device metadata. Must produce 1-2 bullet summary + severity tag (low/med/high) + recommended next action (e.g., schedule maintenance, re-calibrate, ignore).
2) Output must be deterministic/repeatable for same inputs (pilot will benchmark).
3) Explainability: include 1-2 tokens of provenance: which metric(s) drove the severity decision (must be human readable).
4) Audit logs: every generated summary must be stored locally and forwarded when network resumes; central console must support retrieval.

Constraints that shape architecture choices
- Hardware: many edge boxes run ARM64 with 4GB RAM but 1.5–2GB often reserved for OS + aggregator; available for model ~1.0–1.6GB.
- Power & thermal: sustained 100% GPU-style workloads not possible; model must be low CPU and light memory.
- Tokenization: streaming and large prompt context are expensive; prefer compact structured inputs (feature vector -> prompt template).

Options evaluated (pros/cons quick sketch)
A) On-device tiny quantized LLM (float16->int4/int8) running locally (Redwood Private package / small runtime).
   - Pros: meets privacy, low uplink, can run offline, simplest UX for customers.
   - Cons: model engineering + quantization risk (quality regressions), memory fit tight, initial throughput may exceed device CPU budget (latency risk).

B) Near-edge lightweight gateway (small VM per cluster of devices) running a larger quantized model with strong CPU/GPU (Redwood Dedicated or Private in customer's colo).
   - Pros: better model quality, faster inference (if GPU available), easier to update/rollback, central metrics.
   - Cons: requires regional infra footprint, not fully offline for individual devices, network hop adds latency and potential single point of failure.

C) Hybrid: on-device simple rule+small LLM fallback to gateway for ambiguous cases.
   - Pros: best cost/quality tradeoff, graceful degradation, reduces gateway load.
   - Cons: added complexity, policy sync logic needed.

Immediate technical gotchas called out in discussion
- Tokenization overhead: converting structured vectors into natural language prompts adds tokens; better to use structured function-calling style if we keep on-host. Must validate token counts for per-inference cost and latency.
- KV cache warm-up: many of the anomalous events are prefix-similar; need prefix caching at gateway to benefit from per-device session reuse. But devices may not have long lived sessions.
- Quantization fidelity: initial tests with 7B->int4 caused hallucinated severity reasons (false positives). Need eval harness with domain-specific ground truth and adversarial prompts.
- Failure modes: offline generation failing silently — ensure local queue + persisted failure indicator and telemetry.
- Observability: customer asked for per-device cost/latency line items in console. Work with product to surface token-level cost for gateway requests.

Redwood-specific implementation notes (quick)
- Private deploy option: suggest starting with a small Private control plane inside Marlowe VPC. Deploy near-edge gateway nodes in each regional cluster (Chile / US) as Dedicated pools sized for expected peak.
- On-device runtime: recommend attempting a 1.3B-3B quantized candidate that fits RAM; baseline model candidates: open-llama-1.3b-quant, mpt-1.3b-quant (bench first). Use small-context prompting + function schema output.
- Fallback policy: if on-device model confidence < threshold or output length > configured token limit, forward to gateway with original inputs + last n tokens (n small).

Dataflow (textual)
- sensor -> aggregator (pre-transform) -> on-device model attempt (generate summary) -> store local log + send alert if severity >= med -> when network available sync local logs to regional gateway -> gateway aggregates and sends batches to central console.

Evaluation plan and metrics for pilot
- Run A/B across 50 devices for 4 weeks: 25 with on-device model A (1.3B quant), 25 with hybrid policy. Measure: summary accuracy vs human-labeled ground truth (precision/recall for high-severity), response P95 latency, bytes uplink reduction, monthly compute cost.
- Success criteria to move to scale: >= 60% reduction in uplink + precision for high severity >= 0.85 and P95 latency <1.2s (on-device).

Action items (owners + rough dates)
- SOFIA: produce lightweight eval harness (domain prompt sets + label ingestion) + share by 2025-09-10. [owner: Sofia Li]
- MARCUS: spin up two quantization experiments (1.3B int8, 3B int4) on AWS ARM runners; collect quality/latency by 2025-09-17. [Marcus Patel]
- ELENA: draft hybrid fallback policy spec + quick state sync protocol (pseudocode) by 2025-09-12. [Elena Rodriguez]
- MARLOWE (Priya): provide 2 months of anonymized sample telemetry (with device metadata) and 20 labeled anomalies for eval by 2025-09-09. [Priya Sen]
- Ops: add a console card request for per-device token/cost lines (product ticket) and link to pilot JIRA-AG-2143. [TBD]

Open questions / decision points (need answers before infra work)
- Will customer accept an on-device black-box model for initial pilot, or must we provide human-readable provenance for every decision? (Tom to confirm with compliance team)
- Can Marlowe provision a regional gateway VM (lightweight) in each region? If yes, gateways could centralize logging and reduce per-device cpu needs.
- SLA: what are acceptable retry/backoff windows for local logs? (customer hinted 12-24h)

Notes to self (scratchy)
- Prioritize reproducibility in prompts: use structured outputs (JSON/function call) vs free text to make evaluation easier.
- Build small CLI tool to inject synthetic anomalies to device and capture end-to-end latency (need to include battery level sim).
- Risk: if model sizes don't fit, fallback plan is rule-based thresholding + send raw compressed window to gateway for heavier model scoring.

References / useful links (internal)
- Similar pilot: "ridgecrest-insurance-inference-onboarding" for private-deploy sync pattern (see Confluence).
- Quantization notes: internal doc "quantization-compact-runtimes-2025" (Marcus draft).

Next sync: 2025-09-10 10:30 PT (stand up to confirm data delivery + initial quant results).

End of note.
